body.title: design.story LLDs can propose rebuilding existing surfaces that s1 analyze already surfaced
body.reproduction: Run triage -> standalone design.story on a request touching an existing component (observed: E202611031bd72813, multiple concurrent chats). s1 context.assemble runs insrc_analyze_step and the bundles name the existing surface (docs-review-panel.ts exports incl. createDocsReviewHost; the file was even flagged as the top tab-identity resolver candidate), yet the emitted LLD modeled the docs-review panel as having no existing tab keying seam and proposed building in-panel presentation instances - rebuilding what already exists. Expected: the current-behavior section states the existing panel/host and the change reuses it. Observed: the mis-model survived until the daemon review current-behaviour check (round 1) and a user clarification.
body.rootCause: s1 (context.assemble) only produces analyze bundles; no later design.story step (s4 contract.detail, s8 checklist.verify) requires an explicit existing-surfaces reuse inventory grounded in those bundles, nor fails when a proposed new component matches an already-exported surface. Discovery surfaces the fact; nothing consumes it as a constraint.
body.fixIntent: Add an explicit existing-components reuse inventory requirement to the design.story synthesis (grounded in s1 analyze bundles) and make s8 checklist.verify fail when a proposed new component matches an existing exported surface in the bundles. Prompt/checklist text + tests only; no runtime or daemon change.

citations.quotedText: s1 context.assemble prompt requires insrc_analyze_step for every code claim and emits analyzeBundles[] - but no later step must reconcile them as reuse targets.

Bundle names docs-review-panel.ts (43 entities, 12 exports incl. createDocsReviewHost) as top tab-identity resolver candidate, yet its summary says the profiles do not establish review-tab identity rules.
